issues.title: Perfect hash join for RIGHT joins v2 (all 3 gates)
issues.hypothesis: q13 is now the largest template (785.6ms, 17.1% of total). Its plan is customer LEFT JOIN orders, run as a RIGHT HASH_JOIN with customer (1.5M dense unique c_custkey) as the build side. That join took about 1.8s CPU. The perfect HJ is never used here, because of three gates I verified in the code: (1) perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:73 requires join_type==INNER. (2) join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:275 computes compute_aggregates_anyway only for INNER joins. The probe keys sit behind a compress projection, so probe_info is empty and the join gets no build min/max. (3) perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:115 bails when ht.Count() > build_range. A fully dense key set has range+1 keys, so this off-by-one rejects every fully dense build, including INNER ones. A previous run fixed all three and measured q13 -20% (join operator 1.87s→0.19s CPU).
issues.plan: 1) In src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp near line 275, allow compute_aggregates_anyway for RIGHT joins too, as well as INNER. Single condition, equality, same conditions as today. 2) In src/execution/operator/join/perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp: (a) CanDoPerfectHashJoin at line 73 should accept JoinType::RIGHT alongside INNER. (b) Fix the dup check at line 115 to `ht.Count() > build_range + 1`. (c) RIGHT builds keep NULL-key rows in the HT with has_null=false, so the build fill must check key validity and skip NULL keys. Those rows still have to be emitted by the RIGHT scan as unmatched. (d) Track RIGHT-join matches. Mark found_match in a per-slot byte array during probe, then flush it into the HT rows' found_match field before the outer scan (PrepareScanHT / the full-outer scan path in physical_hash_join.cpp). The previous run measured this at -17.8%, against -11.6% for writing found_match into rows directly at probe time. Make sure the existing RIGHT-join outer-scan code in physical_hash_join.cpp still emits unmatched build rows. Keep MAX_BUILD_SIZE as it is.
issues.expected_gain: q13 -15..-20% (about -1.5% geomean). Fixing the off-by-one may also help INNER joins on fully dense dimension keys in q02, q05 and q08 (nation, region, supplier).
issues.generality: FK joins against dense-key dimension tables with outer semantics (LEFT JOIN fact-to-dim, or dim-to-fact planned as RIGHT). Fully dense INNER builds also gain from the off-by-one fix. Downside: a sparse range close to MAX_BUILD_SIZE could cost more memory, but the existing range cap still applies.
issues.risk: Medium. RIGHT-join correctness for unmatched rows and NULL build keys is the main risk; bench results checks should catch it. The optimizer change only adds min/max aggregate computation for RIGHT joins.

## Memory (gen1)

## State
- r1: E0001 JoinDependentFilterRule before DistributivityRule ACCEPTED: q19 -46%, geomean -4.2%.
- r2: E0002 contains()/LIKE length-aware selectivity ACCEPTED: q09 1227→763 (-37%), geomean -3.9%. Best is now 1.087x.
- r3 DISPATCHED: Perfect HJ for RIGHT joins v2 (3 gates + per-slot match bytes). Target q13.
- Current top templates: q13 786ms (17%), q09 764, q18 699, q04 315.
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run on this same codebase/workload. Treat them as strong measured priors, not as already-landed code. Read the specific memory .md files directly with Read; cd+cat in Bash gets blocked.

## Prior-run wins to port, in rough priority order (gain / risk)
1. DONE r1: JoinDependent rule reorder.
2. DONE r2: contains selectivity.
3. r3: Perfect HJ RIGHT. Gates verified: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:73 (INNER only), :115 (off-by-one, Count > build_range), join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:275 (compute_aggregates_anyway INNER only).
4. Substring prefilter over contiguous string runs (LIKE/contains): q13 -11%. SIMD strstr needs an overlapping tail. FSST batched decode q13 -4..-7%.
5. Join key-set range filter through compress projections: q18 -13.6%. Semi-join RHS-aware estimate: q18 -8%.
6. Redo the q09 profile first (the plan changed after r2; lineitem may have lost its BF). Then: BF on first key of a multi-key HJ (q09 -21%), join filter through CM compress (q09 -8%), exact bitmap BF for dense int keys (q09/q16/q21 -10..-15%).
7. Large perfect HA (22-bit) + parallel source: q13 -18.6%. Distinct HT partitioned on group hash: q16 -12%.
8. OR-of-ranges as ExpressionFilter, dense mask eval: q19 -7..-11%.
- q04 (315ms) has no prior idea; it is worth profiling once the ports run out.

## Known dead ends (prior run)
- HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ, bitpacking select: all ~0%.

## Codebase facts
- Rule registration order lives in src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp (rewriter.rules push_back).
- Scan-filter cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::ExtractGetStats → InspectTableFilter (relation_statistics_helper.cpp). It now has an EXPRESSION_FILTER case for contains/like.
- q04 shows ±7-11% bench noise; ignore single-run q04 moves.
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read the memory/ledger and dispatch the next prior win quickly.
